stem: After how many days will the crew have planted a total of 455 sedge plugs?
stimulus: A wetland restoration crew has already planted 140 sedge plugs along a stream bank. Starting today, the crew plants 35 more plugs each day.
explanation: Write $140 + 35d = 455$. Subtract 140 from both sides to get $35d = 315$, so $d = 9$. After 9 days the crew will have planted 455 plugs.

B.why: You divided the total by the daily rate, $455 \div 35 = 13$, and forgot to subtract the 140 plugs that were already planted.

C.why: You added the starting amount instead of subtracting it: $(455 + 140) \div 35 = 17$.

D.why: 315 is how many plugs are still left to plant. You stopped before dividing by 35 to turn that number into days.

stem: How many slides did the lab prepare for the researcher?
stimulus: A paleobotany lab charges a one-time setup fee of $\$75$ plus $\$25$ for each thin-section slide of petrified wood it prepares. A researcher's total bill was $\$400$.
explanation: Write $75 + 25s = 400$. Subtract 75 to get $25s = 325$, so $s = 13$ slides.

B.why: You divided $\$400$ by $\$25$ and never took out the $\$75$ setup fee, which is charged only once.

C.why: You added the setup fee to the bill instead of subtracting it: $(400 + 75) \div 25 = 19$.

D.why: $\$325$ is how much the researcher paid for slides. The question asks how many slides, so you still need to divide by $\$25$.

stem: After how many laps will 500 milliliters of water remain in the pack?
stimulus: During an endurance trial, a sports scientist fills an athlete's hydration pack with 1,500 milliliters of water. The athlete drinks 125 milliliters of water per lap.

A.why: You divided the 500 mL that remains by 125. The 500 mL is what's left, not what the athlete drank.

C.why: $1{,}500 \div 125 = 12$ is the number of laps until the pack is empty. The question stops at 500 mL left, not 0 mL.

D.why: 1,000 mL is how much water the athlete drinks. The question asks for the number of laps.

stem: If the linguist continues at this rate, after how many more weeks will the lexicon contain 500 entries?
stimulus: A linguist began building a lexicon of an endangered language 6 weeks ago. The lexicon now has 230 entries, and the linguist adds 18 new entries each week.
explanation: Starting from today, write $230 + 18w = 500$. Then $18w = 270$, so $w = 15$ more weeks.

A.why: You subtracted the 6 weeks already spent from the correct answer, $15 - 6$. Those weeks are already counted in the 230 entries the lexicon has now.

C.why: 21 is the total number of weeks since the project began, $6 + 15$. The question asks how many more weeks.

D.why: 270 is how many entries are still needed. You still have to divide by 18 to get weeks.

stem: If the society spends its entire budget, how many copies of the field guide does it buy?
stimulus: A folklore studies society has a budget of $\$540$ for a storytelling-collection project. It buys one audio recorder for $\$120$ and spends the rest of the budget on copies of a field guide that cost $\$15$ each.

B.why: You divided the whole $\$540$ by $\$15$ and forgot that $\$120$ of the budget goes to the recorder.

C.why: You added the recorder's cost to the budget instead of subtracting it: $(540 + 120) \div 15 = 44$.

D.why: $\$420$ is the amount spent on field guides. The question asks for the number of copies.

stem: How many hours after cooling begins will the kiln reach 420°C?
stimulus: In a materials science lab, a kiln holding ceramic test tiles is at 1,140°C when cooling begins. The kiln's temperature then drops at a constant rate of 60°C per hour.

A.why: You divided the target temperature, 420°C, by the rate. The quantity to divide is the total drop in temperature.

C.why: $1{,}140 \div 60 = 19$ is the time to cool all the way to 0°C, not to 420°C.

D.why: 720 is how many degrees the temperature falls. The question asks for hours.

stem: If the musicologist continues at this rate, by the end of which week will a total of 240 manuscripts be catalogued?
stimulus: A musicologist is cataloguing a composer's handwritten scores at a constant weekly rate. By the end of week 2, 60 manuscripts had been catalogued. By the end of week 5, 120 manuscripts had been catalogued.
explanation: The rate is $(120 - 60) \div (5 - 2) = 20$ manuscripts per week. From week 5, write $120 + 20w = 240$, so $w = 6$ more weeks, which means the total is reached at the end of week $5 + 6 = 11$.

A.why: 6 is the number of extra weeks after week 5. The question asks which week it is, so you need to add those 6 weeks to week 5.

B.why: You used 60 manuscripts per week as the rate, forgetting to divide the change by the 3 weeks between the data points. That gives 2 more weeks, so week 7.

D.why: 120 is how many manuscripts are still left to catalogue after week 5. It isn't a week number.

stem: What is the length, in meters, of each of the other two sides of the basin?
stimulus: A civil engineering firm is designing a rectangular stormwater retention basin. The perimeter of the basin must be 260 meters, and two opposite sides of the basin are each 75 meters long.

B.why: You subtracted only one 75-meter side before halving: $(260 - 75) \div 2 = 92.5$. Both 75-meter sides count toward the perimeter.

C.why: 110 is the combined length of the two unknown sides. You still have to divide by 2 to get one side.

D.why: You subtracted one 75-meter side from the perimeter and stopped there. A rectangle has two of each side length.
